image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Move above the isolated chip using current head geometry; level the open gripper before descending.
Finish centering above the chip while beginning a shallow open-gripper descent.
Descend vertically with fingers open; the chip is centered in the wrist view.
Continue the open vertical approach, retaining the visually centered lateral position.
Slow the final descent to grasp height; keep the fragile chip untouched by the open fingers.
Make a small visual centering correction and close only through free space, leaving margin before chip contact.
Approach contact gradually with a millimeter lateral centering adjustment; monitor both tactile views before tightening further.
Close in very small increments near the chip edges, then pause to check tactile contact without over-compressing.
Tactile views remain clear; narrow the aperture gradually toward this smaller chip, keeping the hand stationary.
Continue closing at a reduced rate, checking for the first tactile edge impressions rather than squeezing fully.
One fingertip now shows light contact; narrow only slightly and pause to seek bilateral support without crushing.
Balance the slightly off-center edge contact with a half-millimeter lateral correction, then close minimally.
Gently reduce aperture toward bilateral contact; avoid lifting until both edges appear supported.
Both tactile views now show edge contact. Keep the gentle aperture fixed and perform a small vertical retention check.
The chip rose with the gripper and retains its shape and tactile contacts. Continue a gentle vertical lift at unchanged aperture.
Lift farther for tray-rim clearance, maintaining the light grip and monitoring unchanged chip/tactile appearance.
Complete the clearance lift before translating to the tray; chip remains visibly retained at the unchanged opening.
Begin a smooth lateral transport toward the visually located tray, keeping the chip level and the gentle grip fixed.
Continue level transport across the clear space toward the tray; wrist and tactile views show retained chip contact.
Maintain clearance and the unchanged gentle aperture while moving toward the tray center.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Continue level transport with no rotation and unchanged gentle opening.
Resubmit corrected translation-only commands from the unchanged observation; maintain grip and clearance.
Approach the current tray center at clearance height, retaining the unchanged light grasp; chip and tactile contacts remain stable.
Finish aligning the retained chip over the tray using current head and wrist views; keep clearance and the gentle aperture unchanged.
Chip is visibly retained and aligned above the tray. Begin a level vertical descent while preserving the gentle grasp; do not release before support.
Continue descending over the tray center, slowing near the support surface. Preserve the existing light grip.
Lower the intact, retained chip slowly toward the tray floor. Keep both finger contacts unchanged until stable tray support is evident.
Slow the final approach to the tray floor, preserving the light grip. Support is not yet visually certain, so do not release.
Ease the chip another two millimeters toward the tray support surface, maintaining its gentle grasp and checking for settling before release.
Continue the submillimeter seating approach and pause with the grip unchanged; verify tray support before opening.
Ease downward another fraction of a millimeter with unchanged light grip, watching for seating or contact changes before release.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged pose. Lower only 0.6 mm and pause, preserving the gentle grip while checking tray seating.
The chip appears seated against the tray floor. Hold its pose and gentle aperture to let support settle before opening, without pressing farther.
The chip remains settled against the tray after the pause. Gradually open the fingers at fixed height, leaving the tray to support it without lifting or pushing.
The chip remains intact in the tray with tactile contact cleared. Finish opening at fixed height and allow it to settle before retracting.
Retract vertically with fingers open. The released chip remains visibly intact on the tray; verify it stays supported as the hand clears.
Continue clearing the tray vertically with open fingers. The chip stays on the tray with its shape intact and both tactile views clear.
Finish the gentle withdrawal and hold clear of the tray. The chip remains visibly intact and stationary on the tray after release.
